scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Oppana is a traditional form of social entertainment deeply rooted in the cultural life of the Mappila Muslim community of Kerala, South India, particularly throughout the Malabar region.
The term is believed to originate from the Arabic word 'Affna' or 'Afna'.
Historically performed during major family rites of passage, Oppana has evolved beyond private domestic spaces.
on_screen: Map: India · South Asia
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: While Oppana is most famously associated with Mappila weddings, it is also performed during other major family and life-cycle events within the Mappila community.
These include circumcision ceremonies, a girl's first menstruation, and the ritual bath following childbirth.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Oppana is generally presented by a group of about fifteen women, which includes both dancers and musicians.
The bride, dressed in fine attire, adorned with gold ornaments, and decorated with intricate mylanchi (henna) patterns on her hands and feet, sits on a central chair known as a peetam.
She acts as the chief spectator while the dancers form a circle around her.
Watch for Oppana chayal, Oppana murukkam.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (ampQdhHjNmA)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Circular formation centered around a seated individual on a peetam.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The dance is driven by Mappilapaattu, traditional songs composed in Arabi Malayalam—a unique linguistic blend of Arabic and Malayalam.
The lyrics frequently touch upon themes of married life, gently teasing the couple and highlighting the shyness of the bride.
Listen for the Harmonium, Tabla, Ganjira, Elathaalam.
A vibrant blend of vocal call-and-response in Arabi Malayalam supported by harmonium melodies, steady tabla and ganjira drumming, sharp elathaalam cymbals, and rhythmic hand clapping.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: The central focal point of Oppana's setting is the bride on her peetam, elaborately dressed and covered in gold jewelry with her palms and feet decorated with mylanchi.
The surrounding dancers dress in coordinated festive attire suitable for a Mappila celebration.
The setting is traditionally a domestic courtyard or hall, though modern performances frequently take place on auditorium stages.

scenes.title: The people
narration: There are two structural styles of Oppana: Oppana chayal (performed without hand clapping) and Oppana murukkam.

Oppana developed as a social entertainment form within the Mappila Muslim community of Kerala, deriving its name from Arabic roots ('Affna'/'Afna') and incorporating Arabi Malayalam musical traditions (Mappilapaattu).
